No lineage digest, no masked-coordinate comparison and no verdict of any kind
has been computed. The rules are fixed before their outcome can be known.

The question: the manuscript says TAP_0 is computed on the initial statistical
completion -- the table the first training round sees -- and that no imputer
sees the complete table; docs/T53_tap_family_rules.md says the family variants
read data/derived_shuffled/{ds}_complete.csv, "the same input the archived TAP
used". If that file is the pre-mask benchmark table, both cannot be true of the
same object, and a comparator would have been fed the values the other side had
to predict.

The decisive test is prespecified here and needs no threshold: on the masked
coordinates, classify every cell as equal to the prespecified fill only, equal
to the withheld truth only, equal to both (the coincidence class), neither, or
missing. A table is CLEAN-COMPLETION only if every masked cell carries the fill
value; LEAKING if any masked cell carries the withheld value where the fill rule
would have produced something else. Float comparison is exact, so a near-miss
lands in the visible "neither" class rather than being absorbed by a tolerance.

The instruction's decision tree is binary. It is refined here into PASS /
SCOPED-DEFECT / FAIL, because a defect confined to the T5.3 sensitivity family
has a different consequence from one on the primary comparison chain. The
refinement is declared now so it cannot be chosen after seeing the numbers.

if SNI-D's median cross-seed Spearman is below 0.5, since a tool an order of
magnitude less stable than its own published 0.951 is not the tool the paper
describes.
